title: Youtuber Accidentally Exposes the Scam He's Promoting
summary: Investigation of a crypto 'metaverse' token promoted via a paid streamer event: play-to-earn, staking lock-ups, affiliate tiers, and 10x-100x promises.

assertions.quote: I'm going to label all of this Ponzi nonsense
if you ever see a flowchart that seems almost impossibly complicated uh it's Ponzi nonsense

verdicts.note: A reasonable heuristic rather than a tested rule.
In the MLM setting Taylor says complex compensation plans obfuscate the income distribution and hide the near-zero odds of profit; supports the heuristic for MLMs only.

assertions.quote: advertising 10x to 100x is that a get-rich quick scheme yes or no
this is the streamer I show speed and he's about to accidentally expose the scam he's been paid to promote

verdicts.note: An Empire affiliate was paid $1.5 million to promote the scheme on social media with false success claims; an ecommerce rather than trading or crypto scheme, and disclosure is not addressed.

assertions.quote: the target of most crypto scams is gullible people and who's more gullible than kids and teenagers

verdicts.note: Influencer-promoted tokens targeting young audiences are a documented pattern.

assertions.quote: people don't get rich on affiliate program

verdicts.note: Affiliate income distributions are heavily skewed; typical participants earn little.

assertions.quote: the average user can expect to earn up to 20% on staking rewards

verdicts.note: High fixed yields in 2021-22 schemes were funded by emissions and collapsed; some protocols do earn fees.
